add_brands.says: British maker of upmarket furnishing fabrics and wallpaper, founded 1968; included in V&A British Design 1948-2012 exhibition
Family-owned French house since 1935 designing and manufacturing traditional French fabrics, carpets and rugs; owns Braquenie, Boussac, Fadini Borghi, Le Manach
Historic French textile and carpet brand now owned by Pierre Frey (harvest dropped it for weak source; this page names it)
French silk-weaving brand (Tours) owned by Pierre Frey
Furnishing fabric house founded 1930s by Sibyl Colefax, joined by John Fowler 1938; English country-house chintzes; group also owns Manuel Canovas, Jane Churchill, Cowtan and Tout, Larsen
French fabric house (toiles de Jouy) owned by Colefax Group
Founded 1970 by Tricia Guild; furnishing fabrics, bed and bath; Queens Award for Export 1996, Elle Decoration Best British Brand 2010
Venetian weaving mill (Trapolin lineage, called in 1897 the oldest and most renowned in the Veneto); fabrics for La Scala, Bolshoi; Elle Deco International Design Award 2024
Est. 1921, last operating textile factory in Venice; fabrics handmade with Mariano Fortuny techniques; also throws and cushions
Since 1752, one of the oldest Lyon furnishing-fabric manufacturers, family-run 9 generations, silk velvets and brocades on hand looms
Venetian artisanal weaving workshop; soprarizzo velvet still handwoven on 18 eighteenth-century looms from the Venetian silk guild
Maison since 1914, leader in high-end furnishing fabrics and bespoke rugs; brands Quenin (1865), Tassinari & Chatel (1680)
Lyon silk mill with origins in 1680 Pernon workshop, supplier to Louis XV; hand looms; among first EPV-labelled firms (2006)
Danish textile company est. 1968, design textiles, rugs and window coverings; own mills in England, Norway, Netherlands; 10-year warranty on most textiles
One of Swedens oldest weaving mills, family-run since 1692, woven in Horred; known for quality linens: tea towels, tablecloths, runners, blankets
Wool blankets since 1940 from Norwegian wool, 100% Norwegian production; described as one of the most renowned all-Norwegian quality products
Linen weaving mill in Halsingland (historic Swedish linen region), founded 1990; 100% Swedish-made pure linen towels, dishcloths, table linen
Founded 1820 in Tampere; once the Nordics largest industrial firm; describes itself as the most popular and loved textile manufacturer in Finland (bed linen, towels)

Founded 1946 (Sonnenberg and Joe Hunter) to mass-produce lightweight aluminium venetian blinds; inventor of Duette honeycomb, Luminette, Pirouette shades; Levolor Wikipedia page calls it the Dutch custom window blind manufacturer that bought Levolor (2016). Source is a dealer history page
American window blind maker founded 1914 in Hoboken by Hans Lorentzen, who introduced standardisation and assembly lines to the blind industry; venetian-blind icon
Swiss, founded 1952; pioneered the first silent curtain track, curved tracks and push-button electric curtain operation; high-end curtain tracks and blinds
Marrakech rug maker; Carpet Design Awards 2023 finalist (Ourika Valley, Best Modern Design Superior)
Beijing rug maker; CDA 2023 finalist, Best Modern Design Deluxe (M/M (Paris) for TAN)
Sydney rug house; CDA 2023 finalist Best Collection (Supergraphics)
Istanbul; CDA 2023 finalist Best Flatweave (Flow)
Helsinki; CDA 2023 Sustainability finalist (Typewriter Collection)
Italian rug house; CDA 2019 finalist Best Modern Design Superior (Magia in Fog)
Repeated CDA finalist (2019: Balouch LightPink in finest Persian weave, Portland House, magazine; 2020: EasyMe, NewTribal per rugnews shortlist)
CDA 2019 finalist Best Transitional (Ghom Copper, traditional Persian design woven by Iranian weavers)
CDA 2020 shortlist, Best Transitional (Shehnameh) and Best Flatweave (Sixth Sense)
CDA 2020 shortlist in three categories (Moon Collection, Purple Abrash flatweave)
CDA 2020 shortlist Best Modern Design Deluxe and Best Transitional
CDA 2020 shortlist Best Modern Design Select (Feathers Round by Maarten De Ceulaer)
CDA 2020 shortlist Best Modern Design Select (Plumes)
Wikipedia: the most famous workshop in Isfahan, some pieces exceed 1,000,000 knots/sqm; carpet-collector.com: family workshops since 1940, arguably the most sought-after name in fine Isfahan carpets

Shiraz/Zurich family firm since 1947 ("Father of the Gabbeh"); hand-spun, naturally dyed Zagros wool woven by Ghashghai and Luri nomads; Home Textiles Today: three Carpet Design Awards in 2009; repeated CDA finalist 2019/2020

Azerbaijani carpet-weaving union founded 1927 (state OJSC since 2016); 14 studios, ~500 rural women weavers; Guba-Shirvan, Gazakh-Ganja, Garabagh, Tabriz collections; Azerbaijani carpet UNESCO-listed 2010
Named with Artsakh Carpets as Armenias biggest historical carpet producers
Founded 2013 in Stepanakert, ~100 staff at 5 sites, rugs typical of Karabakh (dragon and eagle motifs); now displaced
Carpet company of collector James Tufenkian, named as actively reviving Armenian carpet weaving
Badghisi family (six generations, Turkmen origin) silk-carpet factory in Samarkand, 450+ staff; mulberry silk with madder, saffron, walnut natural dyes

Works with thousands of Afghan weavers (Bamiyan and elsewhere), designs and finishes contemporary and traditional carpets with the value chain entirely in Afghanistan; took over ARZU Studio Hope weaving centres 2019

Renowned Bangladeshi lifestyle store (BRAC social enterprise, 1978) begun by improving women artisans hand-stitched nakshi kantha quilts; ~65,000 craftspeople; also named by IIAS/Wikipedia among kantha-making organisations. Already A1; add B2 for kantha, homewares

Bangladeshi NGO craft maker named in the kantha revival after Karika and Aarong; its artisans stitched Surayia Rahmans Nakshi Kantha Tapestry for the Sonargaon Hotel, Dhaka; sells nokshi kantha and rugs
Bangladeshi handicrafts cooperative that led the 1970s kantha revival, using kantha motifs on household goods
Surayia Rahmans kantha workshop (after SDUW, 1982) making story-telling nakshi kantha tapestries on silk with hundreds of women
Fair-trade cooperative of West Bengal artisans making kantha quilts (stocked by TOAST)
Delhi maker working with a cooperative of 1,400 kantha artisans in Murshidabad, West Bengal (par tola geometric kantha) and recycled-sari kantha

Thai Silk Company founded 1950 to revive hand-woven Thai silk; world largest producer of hand-woven fabrics; furnishing textiles in 60+ countries. Already A1; add B2 for furnishing fabrics and home textiles
Mae Fah Luang Foundation (royal patronage) craft brand in Chiang Rai: hill-tribe woven textiles and woven tufted carpets, begun to replace opium cultivation
Lithuanias oldest flax mill (1928, Birzai); vertically integrated linen table, bed, kitchen linen and curtains; Masters of Flax Fibre mark; Premiere Vision exhibitor since 2001
Panevezys linen company since 1957, largest linen textile producer in Lithuania and the Baltic states; table, bed, kitchen linen, curtains

Milanese family linen maker since 1867 (six generations), fully integrated Italian production of bed, bath and table linen; hotel linen leader since Turin Expo 1898; first Italian textile firm with OEKO-TEX STeP
Since 1883 (Fagnano Olona); described as the long-standing leader in Italian cotton and linen home linens, table, bed and bath
Portuguese maker (Sorema, since 1974) of luxury bath linens and bath rugs; recognised as one of the finest bath linens in the luxury market
Nara firm since 1716 (Henokiens bicentenary family firm) in handwoven ramie Nara-sarashi; signature Hana Fukin dish cloth from Nara mosquito-net (kaya) cloth won the Good Design Award Gold Prize 2008
Tokyo maker of traditional hand-dyed tenugui cloths (shop since 1987), reviving the tenugui craft
add_brands.dept: Tenugui (flat cloths, kitchen and hand towels)

add_brands.says: Westphalian bedding maker since 1847, specialist in fine down duvets and pillows on own batiste; sold in 40+ countries
Founded 1921 in Wuppertal making handmade quilts; family firm producing duvets and pillows in Germany, Switzerland (Swiss Dream, Dauny) and Hungary; first neck-support pillow

Listed in the Reseau Excellence (EPV network) directory category Rideaux, stores & habillage de fenetres (curtain hardware). Harvest saw it but did not take it for lack of soft-furnishing evidence; this category page supplies it
Listed in Reseau Excellence (EPV network) category Rideaux, stores & habillage de fenetres
Passementerie (curtain trimmings, tie-backs) maker listed in Reseau Excellence category Rideaux, stores & habillage de fenetres
Listed in Reseau Excellence category Rideaux, stores & habillage de fenetres
Weaver listed in Reseau Excellence categories Rideaux, stores & habillage de fenetres and Tisserand
Founded 1867, controlled by the Travancore royal family; over a century making handloom coir mats in Alleppey, Kerala, coir heartland
Coir mat maker since 1862 (Karan Group, with The Alleppey Company since 1927); largest exporter of traditional hand-woven coir mats, mattings and rugs from India
Alleppey coir firm since 1927, part of Karan Group (largest integrated natural-fibre floor-covering factory in Asia)
Zorlu home-textile brand: curtains from 1976, bed linen from 1997; 500 stores in Turkey and 100 abroad by 2009; selected most loved home textile brand 2017 (Valeron is the group upper segment)
Bursa towel maker since 1971, fully integrated from raw cotton; claims 30% of the Turkish home-textile market and 1st in Europe / top 6 worldwide for towels and bathrobes
Founded 1879 by Nowrosjee Wadia; describes itself as a national icon for bed linen in Indian homes for 145 years. In brand index under another category only; add B2
One of the worlds largest home-textile makers (towels, bath mats, rugs, sheets); every 5th towel sold in the US; supplies 100,000+ Wimbledon towels a year; owns Christy, Spaces, Welhome

Australian premium bed linen and towel brand founded 1967 by Claudio Alcorso (Derwent Park, Tasmania); synonymous with high-quality fabrics and Australian design; sold in 43 countries by 1994. Harvest dropped it (weak directory); this page restores it

Finnish textiles and home-furnishings company (1951) noted for printed fabrics used in home furnishings; Maija Isola Unikko print (1964) made it a household name. In brand index as A1/A4 only; add B2 (printed furnishing fabrics, bedding, towels)

Nakshi kantha embroidered quilts and throws
Caucasian hand-knotted pile and flatweave carpets (Azerbaijani carpet UNESCO-listed 2010)
Historic silk furnishing-fabric weaving on hand looms (velvets, damasks, lampas)
Fine Isfahan workshop carpets and Ghashghai/Luri gabbehs
Nara-sarashi ramie and kaya mosquito-net cloth used for fukin kitchen cloths
